subject: Math
question_mathml: <math xmlns='http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML'><mtext>In a fruit basket, there are </mtext><mn>4</mn><mtext> apples and </mtext><mn>7</mn><mtext> bananas. What is the ratio of apples to bananas?</mtext></math>
solution_mathml: <math xmlns='http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML'><mrow><mtext>Step 1: Identify the number of apples (4) and bananas (7).</mtext></mrow><mrow><mtext>Step 2: A ratio of apples to bananas is written as apples : bananas.</mtext></mrow><mrow><mtext>Step 3: So, the ratio is 4 : 7.</mtext></mrow></math>
question_text: In a fruit basket, there are 4 apples and 7 bananas. What is the ratio of apples to bananas?
solution_text: Step 1: Identify the number of apples (4) and bananas (7). Step 2: A ratio of apples to bananas is written as apples : bananas. Step 3: So, the ratio is 4 : 7.

subject: Math
question_mathml: <math xmlns='http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML'><mtext>Which of the following ratios is equivalent to </mtext><mn>3</mn><mo>:</mo><mn>5</mn><mtext>?</mtext></math>
solution_mathml: <math xmlns='http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML'><mrow><mtext>Step 1: To find an equivalent ratio, multiply or divide both parts of the ratio by the same non-zero number.</mtext></mrow><mrow><mtext>Step 2: For 3:5, if we multiply both parts by 2, we get </mtext><mn>3</mn><mo>×</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>:</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>×</mo><mn>2</mn><mtext>, which is 6:10.</mtext></mrow><mrow><mtext>Step 3: Check the options. 6:10 is an equivalent ratio.</mtext></mrow></math>
question_text: Which of the following ratios is equivalent to 3:5?
solution_text: Step 1: To find an equivalent ratio, multiply or divide both parts of the ratio by the same non-zero number. Step 2: For 3:5, if we multiply both parts by 2, we get 3x2 : 5x2, which is 6:10. Step 3: Check the options. 6:10 is an equivalent ratio.

subject: Math
question_mathml: <math xmlns='http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML'><mtext>If </mtext><mn>2</mn><mtext> apples cost </mtext><mtext>£</mtext><mn>1.00</mn><mtext>, how much would </mtext><mn>6</mn><mtext> apples cost?</mtext></math>
solution_mathml: <math xmlns='http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML'><mrow><mtext>Step 1: Find the relationship between the number of apples: </mtext><mn>6</mn><mtext> apples is </mtext><mn>3</mn><mtext> times </mtext><mn>2</mn><mtext> apples (</mtext><mn>6</mn><mo>÷</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mtext>).</mtext></mrow><mrow><mtext>Step 2: Multiply the cost of 2 apples by 3 to find the cost of 6 apples.</mtext></mrow><mrow><mtext>Step 3: </mtext><mtext>£</mtext><mn>1.00</mn><mo>×</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>=</mo><mtext>£</mtext><mn>3.00</mn><mtext>.</mtext></mrow></math>
question_text: If 2 apples cost £1.00, how much would 6 apples cost?
solution_text: Step 1: Find the relationship between the number of apples: 6 apples is 3 times 2 apples (6 ÷ 2 = 3). Step 2: Multiply the cost of 2 apples by 3 to find the cost of 6 apples. Step 3: £1.00 x 3 = £3.00.
